Subject: Registrant data minimization + encoder handshake for Nov webinar

Hi team,

Two asks for the Nov 18 ACME webinar:

1) Registrant data minimization: ACME has asked us to only surface a minimal set of registrant fields to On24/Zoom for the registration-to-stream handoff (email, first name, country). They want no free-text fields forwarded and no company revenue/size fields stored in the streaming layer. Laura — can you confirm the current registration schema export and whether our mapping can drop fields at export time?

2) Encoder handshake and SCTE markers: ACME's broadcast team wants a clearly versioned encoder config and a short checklist for live failover between Zoom RTMP and On24 ingest. Ben — can you prepare the encoder handshake doc (config + expected SCTE cue points) and confirm whether the stream key rotation will break registrant correlation IDs?

I attached the event brief; we'll need a small audit trail to show ACME which fields were forwarded (for their security/compliance team). Proposed next steps: Laura to send a registrant map CSV (only headers), Ben to send encoder checklist + config PDF, then I'll consolidate and send to ACME and On24 for sign-off.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Events Lead, Field Marketing
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Registrant data minimization + encoder handshake for Nov webinar

Thanks Marcus — quick update:

- Registrant export: we currently collect (first_name, last_name, email, company, role, country, campaign_source, custom_questions). I created a redacted mapping that drops last_name, company, role, campaign_source and custom_questions prior to export.
- Attached is registrant_map.csv — it's just the header row and a sample row showing the minimized fields (email,first_name,country,registrant_id).
- Our registration form still collects opt-in for recording release; ACME wants that consent flag passed through. We should map consent -> recording_release boolean only.

Limitations: if ACME later requests name-based personalization in the webinar console, we'll need to reintroduce first/last name to the streaming layer. For now we can keep last_name out and use first_name only for on-screen personalization.

I'll leave this with Ben to confirm the registrant_id format will persist across encoder handshake changes.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Event Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, On24 Support <support@on24.com>, Zoom Prod <zoom-prod@example.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Oct 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Registrant data minimization + encoder handshake for Nov webinar

Folks — attached encoder_config_v2.pdf with the handshake checklist. Key points summarized:

- registrant_id persistence: we'll surface a UUID registrant_id in the metadata of the RTMP event and in the On24 API payload. The registrant_id is the only PII-linked token forwarded; email/first_name/country are sent in the minimal payload.
- key rotation: rotating the stream key will not affect registrant correlation as long as the encoder sends the X-Registrant-ID header in the initial POST and we reconcile by session_start timestamp + registrant_id on the backend. If the encoder rotates mid-session, we will treat as new session and stitch on server-side if registrant_id is present.
- SCTE markers: we will use SCTE-35 markers for chapter cues; I included expected marker offsets and a small test vector (3 markers at pre-roll, 00:10:00, 00:35:00).
- Failover: primary RTMP -> Zoom ingest, fallback -> On24 RTMP. On failover we will include a single-page handshake that contains the registrant_id and minimal metadata to preserve analytics.

Action items:
- Marcus: please confirm ACME is okay with UUID registrant_id + consent flag only.
- Laura: make sure the registrant_map.csv header uses column name registrant_id exactly (case-sensitive).
- On24/Zoom: please confirm ingest headers are supported (X-Registrant-ID and X-Recording-Consent).

Ben Carter
Streaming Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: encoder_config_v2.pdf (stub)

We've routed this to our internal security/compliance and they asked for a simple attestation and a signature. Please send us the registrant_map.csv and encoder_config_v2.pdf (we received the stubs) and a DocuSign release for the recording consent mapping so we can sign off with legal.
